page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c3d server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9B14 cores with 2 threads per core on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

The underlying AMD EPYC processor provides a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. In performance testing, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 2864.18 in stress-ng single-core benchmarks. However, multi-core scaling is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 5734.87 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4217.0.

Memory performance represents a significant bottleneck for this configuration. The Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 10%, with uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measured at 37.53 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 15.4 GB/sec. Consequently, memory-bound operations and database tasks show reduced efficiency, with Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations performing in the bottom 25%. For language model workloads, the instance manages average text generation speeds of 141.04 tokens/sec on small 135M models, but drops to a poor 10.77 tokens/sec for prompt processing on medium 7B models.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated compute allocation, this instance is designed for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints or local storage. It is suitable for single-threaded processing, basic web serving, and lightweight utility scripting. The lack of bundled local storage and modest memory capacity position it as a cost-efficient entry point for dedicated CPU workloads, though users must accept the performance tradeoffs in memory bandwidth and multi-threaded scaling.
